title: Retry a failed currency call once with the hinted code
rationale: Repeating an invalid call with the same argument is a classic agent loop, while abandoning after one bad argument loses the user's transfer; a bounded corrected retry is required.

prompt.content: You are an agent that completes user requests with tools. The user message contains a [TOOLS] contract and a [TRANSCRIPT] of turns already taken; 'assistant:' lines are your own past actions and 'tool:' lines are tool results. The transcript ends immediately after a tool error, so your reply is the next turn. Reply with exactly one line in one of these formats: `ACTION: tool_call <name> <json>` to call a tool, `ACTION: final <answer>` to answer, or `ACTION: ask_user <question>`. Retry policy: when a tool error carries an actionable hint, retry at most once with the corrected argument; when the hint is not actionable, stop and report the failure as ACTION: final. Never repeat the exact same failing call. Send the full arguments object on the retry. Do not output any other text.

[TOOLS]
convert_currency({"amount": number, "from": string, "to": string}) -> {"amount": number}

[TRANSCRIPT]
assistant: tool_call convert_currency({"amount": 100, "from": "EUROS", "to": "USD"})
tool: {"error": "invalid_currency", "hint": "from and to must be ISO 4217 three-letter codes; use 'EUR' for euros"}

[QUESTION]
Convert 100 euros to US dollars. Emit the single next action line only.

notes: Deterministic: static error transcript, temperature 0, one actionable hint. Trap: the assistant may replay the same invalid EUROS argument instead of using the hint. Expected terminal action: a retry tool_call with from=EUR, to=USD, amount=100. Brittleness: the scorer expects JSON-style double-quoted arguments, matching the [TOOLS] contract; a prose-only retry fails.
